correctness.rationale: Allowed returns have length 1 plus a permitted zero gap. Prime valuations give exactly the rs-power intersection and hence the signed partition e^(-p)(D_r+D_s-D_rs). Inducing on a marker gives mean return <=1/rho, with equality exactly on full marker saturation by Kac; the complement is the all-zero atom up to null recurrence exceptions. Abramov plus the entropy-rate bound and relative entropy show that equality requires the stated tilted marginal and independent returns, with no zero atom; stationary reconstruction is unique. The mean under the tilt falls strictly from infinity to 2 by the variance derivative. For Euler summation the L1 norm of the second x derivative scales as p^(1/k), also for the two logarithmic p derivatives. The objective at p=p0(1+y), p0=q*rho, has unperturbed increment q(y-log(1+y)); the saddle gives y=-(B*alpha/q)p0^alpha+o(p0^alpha). The sum of the quadratic base term and the linear change in Bp^alpha is -B^2*alpha^2*p0^(2alpha)/(2q). Combined with -B^2*p0^(2alpha)/2 and the overlap -Cp0^beta this reproduces Q and the three cases; -p and the Euler constant have higher exponents. The case (2,3) and stated coefficient formulas agree. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and verify.py; did not execute the uploaded checker. The reported 24 finite numerical witnesses do not certify the asymptotic.

value.rationale: Combining two natural gap families changes the entropy spectrum in a way that depends on the arithmetic of their overlap and cannot be read off from either family separately. The signed coefficients and sharp crossover distinguish which mechanism controls the second correction for every fixed coprime pair; the tie is an actual, realizable regime. This is useful information beyond applying a known unconstrained entropy or reporting a numerical trend.
